    External MCP Server Catalog - Sweep Log, November 1-15, 2026¶

    Archive for November 1-15, 2026. Discovery passes appear newest first. The current sweep log carries the most recent passes.

    Archive: October 16-31, 2026

    🆕 November 12, 2026 - Midday Sweep (1 New, 1 Guide)¶

    Fired on the 10:00 MST tick, seven hours after the night pass shipped four. The canonical came back set identical to that pass's capture (64,577 raw entries against 64,573, 20,885 distinct keys on both, 0 additions and 0 removals, the whole of the movement being four re-served entries in servers/11), so the window was the feed and the queue once more. The one entry that ships earned it on behaviour rather than on size.

    • Kuotia MCP - Spanish Autónomo Tax, Dated and Sourced - remote Streamable HTTP at https://kuotia.com/mcp, no session, keyless for the four public tools, initialize 200 as Kuotia 1.0.1 on protocol 2025-06-18, registry com.kuotia/kuotia 1.0.1. Nine tools, each declaring its own securitySchemes: four public read-only, four reading a gestoría client's own record behind kuotia:gestoria:read, and one write annotated destructiveHint: true that sends only text the client approved with an idempotency_key. Eight calls were driven, and the finding is the refusal: modelo 303 for 2026-T3 returned a verified deadline of 2026-10-20 with its direct-debit cutoff and an AEAT source, while the same modelo for 2026-T4 returned isError: true with code not_verified, the statutory window "del 1 al 30 de enero del año siguiente" and the IVA law as its source rather than presenting the general rule as the checked date. The estimators were driven to a reproduced control: 30,000 income with 5,000 expenses in Madrid returned 4,570.56 in contributions, 2,775.29 in IRPF and 17,654.15 net, the vendor's own published figures for the same example to the cent, and the RETA call returned tramo 5 between 380.88 and 639.45 as the vendor states. The connected half was measured to its gate instead of driven, and that gate is the mechanic worth knowing: a connected tool called without a connection answers HTTP 200 with isError: true and _meta["mcp/www_authenticate"] carrying error="insufficient_scope", scope="kuotia:gestoria:read" and the protected-resource pointer, so a client reading only the status code shows the operator nothing; the protected-resource document names one authorization server and two scopes and the RFC 8414 document publishes authorization_code plus refresh_token, none as the only client auth method and S256 only.

    Also identified this pass (not catalogued). The closest call of the window is Nock (com.usenock/nock 1.0.0, https://api.usenock.com/mcp), Brazilian B2B prospecting with buying signals, company and people search, enrichment and outreach: a keyless initialize answered 401 with resource_metadata and scope="openid profile email", the protected-resource document named Clerk as the issuer, and the registry record described the product, so the evidence was there and the class was not - the lead-generation slice already carries Leadbay, Vibe Prospecting, VOYGR and Layrcake with AskBond and Skael held inside it, and Brazilian company data was held at Fichário on the regional CNPJ rule recorded against apipj, OpenBase, Corporary and Fuentio. LaunchSpy (io.launchspy/launchspy 1.2.0, published the same day at 14:02Z) answered 401 with missing_api_key off a one-scope protected-resource document over coaches, course creators, their Meta ads, hooks and funnels, and holds on the ad-library class carried by Ad Library Intelligence, Adspy, SpyWinAds and the openadlibrary hold. From the queue, Statuz, Felku Connect, HolicAudit, Cygnix SEO MCP, Dotmira, UTM Watch, VextCAD, YorkerAPI, garmlink, HappyKeywords, okdata, abap-config-mcp, TruthTrail, Sniptide, Crossdrive, while.sh, Rush, StatsPAI, Soko-kun, Pleso Therapy, Vidmoat, Roilo, SightRadar and Loop Marketing were read and held on their class owners, each named in the sweep page. From the feed, deltabridge is threat intelligence, remote-nomad-jobs is the jobs class carried by roTEAMnet and the hiring entries, ctlogs-dev is certificate transparency in the class owned by the catalogued CTlogs.io, alba-design is a design utility, and courio and quo are recorded as unresolved rather than inferred: the mcp.so detail route answers "Only HTML requests are supported here" to a JSON-RPC probe and the reader proxy refused at 401 on bad IP reputation. SealGuard, Aalto, Agent Demand Registry, volatiai and the mambalabsdev fleet carry their previous dispositions.

    🆕 November 12, 2026 - Night Sweep (4 New, 4 Guides)¶

    Fired on the 03:00 MST tick, six hours after the night pass. The canonical surface was flat in a way that can be checked rather than asserted - three raw entries more, zero distinct keys, zero stamps after the cut-off - so the whole window came from the mcp.so feed and the submission queue. All four entries answer a question an operator asks with a spreadsheet, a login or a phone call.

    • Vetto MCP - Fake Signup Checks Before the Account - remote Streamable HTTP at https://usevetto.com/mcp, keyless, initialize 200 as vetto 1.0.0 on protocol 2025-03-26, four tools all annotated readOnlyHint: true, no official registry record found under the name (the search returns a different product). Six calls were driven. check_email on jdoe@gmail.co returned BLOCK with reasons: ["typo", "dead"] and the suggestion jdoe@gmail.com, so an assistant can rescue the customer inside the form; billing@mailinator.com returned BLOCK for role and disposable while team+1@googlemail.com returned ALLOW with freemail and role - a role address alone does not block, which is the ranking that keeps a real team inbox out of the bin; same_inbox proved john.doe+promo@gmail.com and johndoe@googlemail.com are one inbox and kept the control pair apart; check_domains on four domains answered checked: 4, flagged: 2; and how_to_block returned a server-side recipe that tells the caller to fail open on timeout, with the vendor's own 6.2x trial-abuse claim sourced to Stripe and its 800 ms fail-open stated on the page. First signup-integrity entry here.
    • Haven Financing MCP - Borrowing Against a Portfolio - remote Streamable HTTP at https://app.haven.finance/api/mcp, keyless, haven-financing 1.0.0, registry finance.haven/financing 1.0.0, six tools all read-only, four of them driven. A 1,000,000 collateral value and a 200,000 draw on the 12-month term priced to 9,700.20 financing interest plus a 900 fee, 10,600.20 all-in against 17,000 at 8.5 percent, so 6,399.80 saved a year; the same answer carried LTV 20 percent, a 70 percent facility cap, a 50,000 minimum draw and collateralRequiredForDraw: 285,715, with the assumptions printed rather than implied. compare_existing_debt priced all five options at once, the monthly variable line saving the most (7,540.40) and being the only one with no rate lock. The finding is freshness: the rate sheet's asOf is 2026-11-03T20:50Z, nine days before the probe, and its rates sit 5 to 18 basis points below the table embedded in the vendor's own page on the day of reading, so the asOf field is the part to quote. First lending entry here.
    • SplitScanner MCP - Reverse Splits With the Filing Attached - remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.splitscanner.com/mcp, the discovery-open, execution-gated tier: a keyless initialize answered 200 as splitscanner-mcp 0.20.0, a keyless tools/list answered 200 with exactly 24 tools all annotated read-only, and tools/call answered 401 JSON-RPC -32001 Authentication required without an OAuth discovery header, so the subscription boundary is measured and the answers are the vendor's. The tool surface is the argument: split history, lifecycle from proposal to effect, ended and abandoned splits, post-split performance, an authority query with minRemaining and expiringBefore for unused split authority, exchange listing standards, and SEC filing search with document, exhibit and in-text search beside it - every row cited to the filing or notice behind it. Registry com.splitscanner/mcp carries 0.19.0 and 0.19.1 against the 0.20.0 served, and the vendor's limits are quoted as given: scheduled is not confirmed, a missing value is not measured.
    • Tracwell MCP - Analytics Answered Inside the Chat - remote Streamable HTTP at https://tracwell.app/mcp, measured at the OAuth tier: a keyless initialize answered 401 with resource_metadata, the protected-resource document named one authorization server and exactly four scopes (analytics:read, definitions:write, websites:write, offline_access), and the authorization-server document published dynamic registration, code as the only response type, authorization_code with refresh_token, none among the token auth methods and S256 only - so reading analytics is one scope and the two write scopes touch goal and funnel definitions and site configuration, never the event stream. Registry app.tracwell/analytics 1.0.0. The vendor documents the operator controls - only workspace owners approve a connection, the approval names which websites it can see, connections are revoked in Settings, and all MCP access needs an active plan including trials while expired plans keep the dashboard history - and its published plan ladder runs 9 to 149 USD a month with API and MCP access included at every allowance, which is the line worth having. Tool names are vendor statements and labelled as such.

    Also identified this pass (not catalogued). Diffbot (io.github.diffbot/diffbot-mcp, https://mcp.diffbot.com/mcp) is the strongest vendor of the window and is held on its gate rather than on its merit: tool use needs a free Diffbot token, and no free token was provisioned for this pass, so nothing could be measured beyond the submission itself - it is the first target of the next pass with a token. SealGuard (io.github.2cstudiodev-web/sealguard, Solana wallet check-up with a 0-100 safety score) is consumer wallet hygiene, held on the crypto-safety class carried by the x402 and agent-security group. FacturX (com.facturxapi/mcp, Factur-X and ZUGFeRD validation against EN 16931 and the French 2026 rules) is held on the e-invoicing class carried by NormAPI, BeeL and Eleata, and it needs a sandbox key in any case. Toolbox POD (print-on-demand apparel, OAuth with dynamic client registration) and Aalto (an FF&E product library for interior design studios, OAuth with no keyless surface) are both real products that could not be measured past the handshake this pass and are held for a driven session rather than dismissed. Deal.ai is held on the consumer price-comparison class carried by Prickelly, CheapestInIndia and within; OpenCheap (one API across 900+ models) on the model-routing infrastructure class; Agent Demand Registry as a tool directory rather than a data surface; Switchyard and agents-room on the agent-gateway and agent-social classes; Cred402 on the x402 credential class; Scribase Mail and Sendblue on the saturated messaging class; SovaTalk, What's On Vegas and What's On Miami on local events; Neuro-CanvasLMS on education; Dagon Inference, fxapis MetaTrader 5 and Safe Web Reader by class; volatiai-mcp and submission #7176 as empty submissions with no description or tools. The five mambalabsdev entries (#7181 to #7185: Semrush domain metrics, YouTube channel email finder, property-owner records, Ticketmaster event prices, Eventbrite events) are the fourth wave of a fleet now 43 across four waves, held on the standing Apify-actor ruling. From the feed: billdog-io (paywalls, subscriptions and entitlements, OAuth-gated at https://api.billdog.io/mcp with protected-resource metadata) is held for a driven session; twinr (website to iOS and Android apps, 14 tools) on the app-builder class; trainrec as a consumer workout log; internal-ballistics-calculator as a hobby calculator; lampwick on developer monitoring; mentionbird on the AI-visibility class; site-audit-mcp-server and seller-labs-amazon on the Apify and Amazon-seller classes; glen on agent memory; verrow on parcel and zoning data; farside-research on crypto data; blog-automation, glypse, mokxi, ctrl-cv, rentadriver and align-cli by class; and the unstamped rail card set (playwright-mcp, figma-context-mcp, github-mcp-server, pixellab-mcp, next-devtools-mcp, blockbench-mcp-plugin, supabase-mcp) as catalogue furniture rather than arrivals.

    🆕 November 12, 2026 - Midday Supplement Sweep (2 New, 2 Guides)¶

    Fired on the 11:00 MST tick, one hour after the midday pass shipped Kuotia. The canonical was flat to the key and not flat to the stamp - thirteen listings were re-indexed inside the hour and not one of them is a new product - so both entries that ship came from the mcp.so feed, and both are OAuth services with an operator-facing control surface rather than another reporting dashboard.

    • Hank MCP - Who Is On Call, Answered From the Chat - remote Streamable HTTP at https://app.dialhank.com/api/mcp, registry com.dialhank/hank 1.0.0. A keyless initialize answered 401 with resource_metadata; the protected-resource document named two scopes, hank.settings.read and hank.settings.write, and the RFC 8414 document published a registration endpoint, code as the only response type, authorization_code plus refresh_token, none as the only token auth method and S256 only.     Fired on the 03:00 MST tick, six hours after the evening sweep's read. The two surfaces disagreed and both readings are recorded: mcpservers.org was flat to the entry count, every one of its twelve server maps carrying exactly the URL count it carried at 21:00 MST, while the mcp.so feed delivered one scheduled batch of eight cards all stamped 2026-11-11T08:00Z. A crafted message with a duplicated plain-text part, an HTML signature table, a tracking pixel and In-Reply-To headers converted to 465 bytes of Markdown: one body rather than two, the signature preserved as a Markdown table, the date normalised to ISO 8601 UTC from a -0500 header, and the tracking pixel kept by default until --strip-tracking-pixels was passed. --strip-signatures did not remove the table-shaped signature, which is the measured limit of a delimiter heuristic. The licence is the first decision, not the last: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, "any noncommercial purpose is a permitted purpose", no commercial licence published, so an internal company pipeline sits outside the grant. The vendor's own benchmark is labelled as such: roughly 88 percent fewer tokens than raw .eml across an 11-message synthetic set, with the attachment category median about 126,000 tokens raw against 180 converted, and the README says plainly that naive extractors are cheaper because they discard metadata. There is no mailbox connection: it converts files you already exported, and the CLI accepts .zip and .tgz where the MCP tools do not.
    • Vibe Shield MCP - The Security Scan Before an Agent Says Done - npm CLI plus MCP server, zero runtime dependencies, MIT, @vibefoundry/vibe-shield 2.1.2, registry io.github.avivgerz-hue/vibe-shield 2.1.2, repository created 2026-11-07 with 26 stars. On a crafted Next.js App Router route with four planted defects it returned GRADE F, 0/100, 5 critical in 26 ms over 80 active rules: three unguarded mutation routes (VSB-AUTH-001 twice), one concatenated SQL statement (VSB-DB-007), one record owner taken from the request body (VSB-AUTH-004), and one hardcoded credential (VSB-SECRET-001) that the report redacted as sk_liv•••• rather than reprinting it. Exit codes were measured four ways: plain scan 1, --fail-on critical 1, --format json 1, and a clean control file GRADE A+ 0. The JSON report carries schemaVersion, attackSurface, per-finding cwe, owasp, confidence and a remediation object with an insecure and a secure example, and the score object states its own cap: {"ceiling":{"severity":"critical","limit":29}}, so a single critical pins the maximum at 29, which is why the agent-surface audit reported GRADE F, 29/100. That audit is the second command and the honest half of this entry: on a poisoned SKILL.md it caught the exfiltration (VSB-AGENT-002, a curl posting env to a remote host) and the missing manifest scope (VSB-AGENT-010) across 12 rules, and flagged neither "ignore all previous instructions" nor "never mention this section", so it detects what an instruction does, not what it asks a reader to hide. The vendor states its own limit on the demo: "a clean score is not a security guarantee."
    • CtxVault MCP - Memory You Correct Instead of Overwrite - local stdio server and CLI over the same vaults, MIT, package 0.9.1 on PyPI while initialize reports ctxvault 1.30.0, registry io.github.Filippo-Venturini/ctxvault 0.9.1, 62 stars, protocol 2025-06-18. Memory is split into three vault types: semantic documents read by meaning, skill procedures read by name, and episodic statements holding two timelines, valid_from/valid_to in the world and known_at in the vault. tools/list returned 17 tools, more than the eleven the README names, and the episodic set is the design: write_episode, query_episodes (with valid_at, known_at and include_closed), supersede_episode, invalidate_episode, revise_episode, confirm_episode, dispute_episodes, episode_history and list_entities. The lifecycle was run on a throwaway vault: two statements about one customer, one from an invoice and one from a contract amendment, both stayed open, which is the first thing to know because an append corrects nothing by itself; supersede then closed the first at the exact microsecond the replacement opened, kept its source, recorded superseded by pointing at the new record, and deleted nothing. dispute leaves two contradictory statements open rather than picking a winner, which is closer to how an operator treats two sources that disagree. Storage is measured, not inferred: one directory per vault holding one episodes.db, with restricted and allowed_agents in the config, so isolation is a filesystem boundary. The cost is measured too: uv tool install ctxvault occupies 5.9 GB because sentence-transformers and chromadb are hard dependencies that resolve PyTorch and the CUDA runtime wheels on Linux, and an episodic vault builds no vectors unless an embedding model is named at init. Not first of class here, but the first entry where the correction itself is a tool with a closing timestamp.

    • DocPin MCP - Publish an Agent's HTML to a Link You Control - remote Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.docpin.app/mcp, OAuth with dynamic client registration and PKCE, documented from the server's own contract because there is no API key to drive. A keyless initialize answers 401 naming its protected-resource document, and that document answers 200 with exactly 2 scopes, publish and settings, which is the split that decides what a connection can do. The stable link is the entry: republishing a slug puts a new version behind the same link, and around it sit the four capabilities nobody on the artifact shelf combines - set_access with team, public, password, people (emails and @domains) or inherit, version history with restore_version, get_page_views reporting by whom on a people-only page, and a per-page JSON store that set_page_data updates without republishing. Sharing a draft requires an access value, so the agent has to ask who should be allowed in. Page data is capped at 1 MB and about 30 writes a minute; upload links live 15 minutes and take 25 MB; drafts preview for about an hour and are not for sharing. Free is 3 pages, Pro $8 a month adds unlimited pages, custom domains and password or people-only pages.
    • AgentKeyGate MCP - A Pass Instead of the API Key - self-hosted gateway, Apache-2.0, Node.js 22, Streamable HTTP at https://{host}/mcp behind a gwa_... agent token, 1.0.2 in the registry. The agent never receives the service key: it asks for a pass with a ttl and a call count and a reason up to 200 characters, a person approves in Telegram or on the web with those facts in view, and the pass gwt_... dies when the clock or the calls run out. The data filter is why it earns the guide: types and fields are chosen explicitly and everything else is cut from the JSON before it reaches the agent, readOnly is on by default for CRM and support keys, blocked writes do not consume quota, and mask replaces e-mails, separated phones, Luhn-valid cards and IBANs. The vendor's own example: a Bitrix24 lead returns seven fields and the agent gets ID, STATUS_ID and OPPORTUNITY. Weakening a filter needs a fresh TOTP code and shows a "was, now" page first. Recorded honestly: 0 stars, created 2026-11-05, single owner, no external audit, root on the server reads every key, filtering exists for four services, and the vendor's own Checked live column reads no on every client snippet including the Hermes one.

    • ProveCart MCP - Agent Order Checks Before Payment - remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.provecart.com/mcp, keyless initialize 200 as provecart 1.0.2 with all 10 tools listed, and the evidence tier stated rather than implied: provecart_scoreboard and provecart_certification_info were called live and returned real payloads, while the three check tools refuse without an integrator key in the X-API-Key header and say so in one sentence, so the check payload is schema-read and not measured. provecart_check_order, provecart_check_booking and provecart_check_reservation compare what the agent built against the customer's own mandate and return a signed MATCH, REVIEW or BLOCK verdict before the payment is captured, with a non-MATCH answer carrying the Agent Correction Format - a corrections array of dimension, action, expected, actual, reason, a retry budget and a sealed evidence pointer. The mandate is the part that makes this different from a prompt: the order mandate carries 18 structured fields including max_total_price, merchant_allowlist, merchant_blocklist, max_quantity, variant_constraints, price_basis, expires_at and a period_budget with its own window, the booking mandate 26 including airport_substitution, date_flex_days, fare_terms, max_connections, min_connection_minutes and max_layover_minutes, and the reservation mandate 17 including time_tolerance_minutes, party_size_max, max_deposit and cancellation. The scoreboard read live is the argument for the exam: two agents at 100.0 over 29 checks with certification CURRENT to 2027-02-02, and two audit probes at 13.8 and 11.1, with origin separating external, house and audit runs. The rules read live: 80 or above certifies, a pass is CURRENT for 90 days, status is computed from the sealed record at read time, renewal is a newly generated exam, and a pass produces an Open Badges 3.0 / W3C Verifiable Credential under did:web:api.provecart.com. The limits are in the guide: it never holds or moves money, a verdict gates a payment only where the integrator's code calls the check first, the AI layer cannot overturn a block, business onboarding is a free 90-day pilot rather than a published price, and provecart.com answers 401 to a plain reader-proxy fetch. It earns a guide because the agent-payment neighbours (Agentcard, FiatDock, CoinVello, SnapEX Pay, Spectra) answer whether an agent can spend and how much, and none of them answers whether the order was the one the customer asked for.
    • lookfirst MCP - Human Approval Gate for Agent Writes - a local stdio MCP proxy, Apache-2.0 at github.com/Aethelgard-Systems/lookfirst, installed here from the repository and reporting lookfirst 0.2.1 against a README that still says 0.2.0 pre-1.0. Driven, not quoted: the offline demo was run twice end to end. The approval run returned {"status":"executed","approved_by":"elicitation:mcp","readback":"ok","readback_detail":"read-back matches","blocked":false} and the fake bank balance moved 1,250.00 to 1,129.50 EUR for a 120.50 EUR transfer; the denial run returned "status":"denied" with the failed channel named and the balance untouched. Five behaviours are what earn the guide. The decision fails closed and the default table is short: readOnlyHint allows, destructiveHint, an unannotated write and an unknown tool all confirm, and an explicit rule beats the annotation while deny never executes. The approval is bound to the arguments: the webhook answer must carry the per-call HMAC token and echo args_sha256 from the preview or it returns 403, the web page binds its buttons the same way, and every channel shares one timeout where a timeout is a denial. The write is verified by read-back against $args and $result placeholders and reported as ok, unklar or fehlgeschlagen, with structuredContent.lookfirst carrying the verdict so a write is never reported as done on its own word. The log is an Ed25519 hash chain: verify-log walked the run to OK, 20 signed and chained entries, and the demo then rewrote the decision entry and the same command returned TAMPERED, line 6, hash mismatch, with the documented residual (end-truncation plus a deleted .head sidecar) closed by an external --trusted-head checkpoint. The result is masked before the model sees it: the agent received [[IBAN_c30e2f3c...]] and [[NAME_5f082d93...]], passing the placeholder back works because the gate resolves it, and an invented one is refused with Denied: unknown or expired placeholder. The limits are the vendor's own and are in the guide: pre-1.0 with no field record, 0 stars, an autonomous client that auto-answers elicitation approves itself unless confirm.elicitation is off and the page is isolated at the network level, a separate OS user is not enough because every local user reaches loopback, the page has no login and is for 127.0.0.1, an HTTP token is authentication rather than encryption, Windows is untested, and the mask is a deterministic pattern filter that misses split IBANs, zero-width text, Base64 secrets and keys like db_password. It earns a guide because kosa8 isolates the server, TrustScan and AgentTrust judge an endpoint, and glc PromptGuard scores a prompt or an output, and none of them stops one specific write at the argument level, names the human who approved it, verifies the result by reading it back and keeps a chain you can point at.

This entry states its tier rather than implying a session: a keyless initialize returned HTTP 401 with JSON-RPC -32001 Unauthorized. Connect via OAuth or send Authorization: Bearer ***, so the endpoint is live and gated and no tool was called. The data arrives by beacon, not by API: a meta tag plus tracking.js, a no-JS CSS beacon, or a Cloudflare Worker at the edge, with WordPress and GTM installs on Pro+; the vendor is explicit that a meta tag alone identifies the site and records no visits.     • HANRIA Agent Mandate Check MCP - Written Consent Gates - keyless Streamable HTTP at https://check.hanria.ai/v1/mcp, initialize 200 as hanria-check 0.7.4, 2 tools listed and both called, 5 mandate templates read as resources. The operator writes a mandate with a purpose, a default and an ordered clause list where each clause carries an effect of permit, deny or escalate; the agent passes the mandate plus the action it is about to take, and the first matching clause decides. Driven: a three-clause publisher mandate validated to valid: true with a mandate_digest, then four actions. A network post to a https://api.github.com/repos/CorpusIQ/ prefix returned permit on permit-docs-publish; the same verb to another organisation returned escalate with no clause matched and the closest clause named and explained; a transaction pay returned deny on deny-transactions; an administrative grant returned escalate on escalate-admin. Every answer carried a hanria-receipt-v1 receipt with the mandate digest, the action digest, an issue time, a fifteen-minute window and a signature. validate_mandate reports the three failures that make a policy decorative, clauses that can never run because an earlier clause already decides them, unbounded prefixes and credential material, and it proved strict by refusing a first attempt that used kind values of payment and access and a free-text clause field, naming the offending field and the accepted taxonomy of file, process, package, network, device, credential_use, transaction and administrative. It earns a guide because the governance cabinet holds four other pieces and none is a mandate: AgenticRail Gate MCP enforces step order and verifies a receipt chain, AgentLedger MCP caps spend, agent-bom MCP maps an AI supply chain's blast radius and glc PromptGuard MCP scores prompts. The operator-authored authorisation document, with clause ordering and a third escalate outcome, is the piece that was missing.
    • Integrate.io MCP Server - ETL Pipelines by Description - hosted on the account path https://api.xplenty.com/YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID/api/mcp, one JSON-RPC message per request with batch requests refused, OAuth 2.1 or a Personal Access Token, 46 tools per the vendor against 44 on the directory card with the vendor telling clients to run tools/list for the exact set. A keyless POST to an unpopulated account path answered HTTP 401 with Bearer error="invalid_token" and resource_metadata at api.xplenty.com/0/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, so this entry states its tier rather than implying a session. The jobs half is where an operator lives: list_runs, get_run, get_run_summary for records read per source and written per destination, and explain_job_failure for the primary error, the detected patterns and the log tail. The authoring half builds a package from a description, edits components and edges, manages variables, saves a draft and rolls back a version. The containment statements are the part to read first, because mutating tools take effect immediately with no sandbox: mutation-base subclasses accept a dry_run, create_schedule creates a schedule disabled by default, create_cluster provisions billed infrastructure, every change is versioned and audited, list_runs defaults to root runs only so child retries are excluded, and the Personal Access Token default lifetime is ten years, which is the one setting to shorten.     🆕 November 2, 2026 - Midday Supplement (1 New, 1 Guide)¶

    An hour after the midday pass, fired on the 11:00 MST tick, so this is a supplement rather than a second midday read: the window, the feed and the /all page were already dispositioned an hour earlier and are not re-argued here. What changed in the hour is three submissions (Publish MCP #6621, norc #6622, Lingard Vocab #6623) and one reversal with a reason attached.

    • AttriKit MCP - App Attribution That Returns a Decision - stdio through npx -y @attrkit/mcp, published as 2.0.1 on npm with the MIT repository KamyarTaher/attrikit-mcp whose README carries the full 39-tool table, the MCP setup page carrying the same inventory and count, and the pricing page carrying its free allowance in the headline. It is the first entry here that closes the loop from ad spend to app install to subscription revenue to a budget decision. get_campaign_decision returns the attribution engine's call verbatim and the vendor states the model reports it rather than recomputing it; record_campaign_decision stores the scale, cut or hold call with the inputs that produced it, so the call can be graded later once enough results exist, with the vendor's own caveat that a suggestion is not a profit guarantee. Spend is an input rather than a copied dashboard: import_spend takes ad level CSV rows with the paired adset_id/ad_id rule enforced client side since 1.0.0, pull_network_spend reads an authorized ad account, set_cost_model records allocation, and get_spend returns it beside installs and events. RevenueCat joins purchases, renewals and refunds to installs. The delivery rules, the timeouts (15 seconds on most tools, 120 on export_events, import_spend and pull_network_spend), the version 1 export cut at the newest 100,000 events, the one-member workspace, the web SDK not yet on npm and the 25-month retention are all in the guide, as is the pricing read directly: first 10,000 qualified installs free once with no card, then $249 a month including 10,000, then $0.015 each, which prices 50,000 at $849 and 100,000 at $1,599. It earns a guide because Mobzio MCP answers which link produced a marketplace order for a Russian and CIS seller and stops there, while the ad surfaces here stop at the creative (Abyssale MCP, AdTest.AI MCP, Ad Library Intelligence MCP, Adspy MCP, AdMake AI MCP), so no entry in 1,085 guides joined spend to installs and returned a decision with its inputs saved.

    Reversal, stated plainly. The midday pass an hour earlier grouped AttriKit (#6592) with developer tooling and mobile attribution and held it there. That grouping is reversed here on the surface rather than on the vendor: mobile attribution had no catalogued class to be held against (WarpLink was listed as identified and never written up, and Mobzio MCP is marketplace deeplinks for one regional seller set), and the decision and spend tools are an operator surface, not a developer one.     • Royally MCP - WordPress Fleet Changes With Approvals - remote Streamable HTTP at https://app.royally.io/mcp, carried in the official registry as io.royally/royally at version 0.0.898 with status active and statusChangedAt on 2026-11-01T04:1xZ, and answering a keyless initialize with HTTP 401 and {"error":"missing_bearer_token"}, so the surface is live and gated rather than absent. The shape is a cloud command layer plus a plugin on every site, so an agent holds one connection instead of twenty site endpoints. The change flow is the entry: a request is recorded with who asked and which sites it touches, held for approval inside a window that can expire, optionally behind two-person approval and per-site-group rules, applied, and returned as a receipt naming who asked, who approved, what changed on which site and the one click that puts it back, with the receipts collected in a fleet-wide tamper-evident log that exports signed. Safe jobs such as a cache purge after a menu edit are the documented exception and run without the queue. Around that the fleet jobs are worked through the plugins the sites already run: updates with a backup first and automatic rollback, vulnerability and administrator-change alerts through GuardPress, Wordfence or Kadence, backup health through SiteVault or UpdraftPlus, uptime every five minutes with certificate, domain, speed and PHP fatal error checks routed to Slack, Discord or a signed webhook, bulk SEO titles and descriptions and menu and CSS and template copies, WooCommerce prices and stock and orders with a seven-day undo, Elementor builds that wait for approval with a preview link first, SEO audits pulling Search Console and Analytics data through Rank Math and SEOSbolt, and weekly or monthly client reports in the agency's own brand beside a read-only client portal. Pricing read directly: Solo $89 a year for 3 sites and 2 seats, Freelancer $249 for 5 sites and 3 seats, Studio $390 for 25 sites and 5 seats. It earns a guide because every WordPress entry here is single-site, and because it is the first entry in this catalogue that governs other MCP servers rather than only its own tools: its documentation covers connecting the WordPress MCP Adapter, Easy MCP AI and the Elementor MCP behind the same connection under the stated rule that only Royally makes the change, which is supervision rather than a plugin list.

    🆕 November 1, 2026 - Early Sweep (3 New, 3 Guides)¶

    Six hours after the night pass, and the two directories split cleanly: the mcp.so recentServers block put exactly two cards above the 2026-11-01T00:15:52Z stamp, and mcpservers.org carried 30 slugs with the counter at 18,726 against 18,577, every one of them already inside a prior disposition. The movement was in the submission window, where eight submissions landed between #6531 at 04:46:00Z and #6539 at 10:02:34Z. Three shipped, and each was verified on the surface it actually exposes, which for one of them is a keyless read-only sibling server rather than the paid endpoint.

    • Roster MCP - Hire an AI Agent by the Deliverable - remote Streamable HTTP at https://roster-ivory-zeta.vercel.app/api/mcp where the usable half needs no credential: initialize HTTP 200 in 0.23 to 0.55 seconds, serverInfo roster 1.0.0, and tools/list returning all 23 tools with full schemas in 29,165 bytes. The product is a catalogue of named AI agents with a role, a biography, personality sliders, a not_for list and fixed price packages, and the workflow is a purchase rather than a prompt: search_agents on a launch-email brief returned 18 candidates out of the 58 the submission describes, from_price_usd from 30 to 50, turnaround from 60 minutes to 4 hours, and a match_reason written as a sentence. get_agent on the top match returned three packages, $35 for five product pages, $40 for a three-email launch sequence and $50 for one landing page. get_sandbox_key issued a working rk_test_ key with no account, daily_job_limit 20 and spend_limit_usd 100, stating that a sandbox job never reaches a real model and is never billed, and hire_agent with that key returned a completed job in 0.27 seconds with package_selected_by: "brief_match" choosing the three-email package at $40 on its own, the other two returned as alternatives with prices and payment charged: false. get_usage then reported the key's own meter in timezone America/New_York with alert thresholds at 80 and 100 percent. The reason it earns a guide is that nothing else here prices a deliverable before the work starts: a live key is approved by a person through request_access, every key carries a daily job limit and a spend limit, each job includes two revisions, a rating goes on a public track record and open_dispute routes to a human. Gap recorded: no live hire was made, so real turnaround, revision quality and dispute handling are unexercised, and rotate_webhook_secret, redeliver_webhook and signature verification were not driven; sandbox output is a deterministic stand-in, useful as a rehearsal and useless for judging writing quality; and the endpoint is a Vercel deployment domain rather than a custom domain.
    • Markproof MCP - Watermark AI Output for Article 50 - the first entry in this catalogue that treats machine readable marking of generated media as a tool call, and it arrives with a deadline a month away: the European AI Act implementation timeline puts the Article 50(2) obligations for providers generating synthetic audio, image, video or text at 2 August 2026 and requires content placed on the market before that date to be compliant by 2 December 2026. The server is local stdio via npx -y markproof-mcp, MIT, published as markproof-mcp 0.3.1 with mcpName io.github.Ajinkya710/markproof, registering one server with three tools: mark_file, which watermarks and C2PA-signs a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, WAV or MP3 file, writes <name>.marked.png beside the original and returns a watermark code and a public verification URL, with an optional visible AI-generated label; verify_file, which checks any file for a watermark and a manifest and reports signature validity; and get_asset, free, which reads a record by id. The two marking tools cost one API call each. The two layer argument is the correct one: a watermark is a signal in the pixels or the waveform, a C2PA manifest is a tamper evident record that states what generated the file and breaks on any edit, and marking with one and not the other answers half the question. Plans are published plainly, Free at $0 with 250 API calls a month, Indie at $29 for 25,000, Pro at $79 for 100,000, no card for the free key, files processed in the EU, and a free checker at markproof.co/check that needs no signup. Gap recorded, and it is the largest this pass carries: there is no hosted endpoint (https://markproof.co/mcp answered 404) and npx -y markproof-mcp with no key printed set MARKPROOF_API_KEY and exited, so initialize and tools/list could not be run and the three tools are the published package rather than a driven list; watermark robustness, manifest validity, re-encoding survival and the accuracy of verify_file are unverified, the checker was not driven, text marking is outside the server, and https://markproof.co/v1/assets answered 404 from the static site.
    • SeatLayer MCP - Seating Charts Built by an Agent - two servers, and the split is the story. https://mcp.seatlayer.io/mcp answered a keyless initialize with HTTP 401 in 0.28 seconds and {"error":"unauthorized","code":"bad_designer_session"}, the normal state for an OAuth-only surface carrying 63 tools behind a per-administrator grant, while the sibling at https://docs.seatlayer.io/mcp answered 200 keyless with serverInfo seatlayer-knowledge 0.109.1 and 11 tools whose instructions ask the client to quote the canonical URLs every result returns. Three calls were made against it in 0.06 to 0.08 seconds each: pricing returned one prepaid credit per confirmed sold seat with designing, rendering, browsing, holds and releases consuming nothing, the first production payment at $0, 100 free sold-seat credits per organization per calendar month, credits that never expire and a ladder from 500 credits at $50 (10 cents a seat) to 100,000 at $5,000 (5 cents), with hosted ticketing a separate wallet at $0.50 per confirmed ticket paying into the organizer's own gateway; capabilities, reviewed 2026-09-27, separates released from unreleased in the vendor's own matrix with buyer 3D released behind a 2D fallback, 51 templates of which 35 carry 3D relief, and SDKs across web, seven server languages, four mobile platforms and REST OpenAPI 3.1; product_overview records the scale as fixtures rather than adjectives, public demos at a 200,000 seat stadium and a 100,000 seat arena and a readiness observation dated 2026-09-14 on a 53,018 seat chart. The design is why the guide exists: an administrator approves each connection on a consent screen, narrows it to one chart or a workspace and ticks capabilities individually, every call using an event capability re-checks that the person who connected the agent still holds a role allowing it in the dashboard, writing to an event on sale takes a plan the person approves where a yes covers that plan only and held and sold seats never change, an administrator gets a digest at most every 15 minutes per agent, and a publish can be undone in one click. Gap recorded: no grant exists, so all 63 tools are the vendor's documentation rather than a tools/list response, chart building, tracing, validation, publishing and live event control are unexercised, the 200,000 and 100,000 seat demos and the 53,018 seat observation were not loaded, and compare_with and renderer_evidence were not called.

    Integration with CorpusIQ¶

    CorpusIQ is the connector layer that lets AI assistants read the systems a business already runs on - accounting, payments, CRM, email, files and analytics - and answer with the source named. It is read-only by design: it retrieves data and never writes to, or acts in, a connected system, which is what makes it safe to point at live accounts.

    This page is part of the CorpusIQ directory, the reference we maintain for the MCP server and agent-skill ecosystem. Run alongside CorpusIQ, a third-party server like this one can be combined with a company's own business data in a single answer.
